A liquid is heated to ${150}^{∘}\text{C}$ and then left to cool. The temperature of the liquid after $t$ hours is given by $T(t).$  The graph of $T(t)$ is shown above.

Approximate the rate of change of temperature when $t=2$ using a central difference approximation with step size $h=1.$
question.worked_solution:
We use the central difference approximation

$$
{T}^{′}(x)≈\frac{T(t+h)-T(t-h)}{2h},
$$

 
at the time $t=2$ and step size $h=1.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(-1) & ≈\frac{T(2+1)-T(2-1)}{2(1)} \\  & =\frac{T(3)-T(1)}{2} \\  & =\frac{60-120}{2} \\  & =\frac{-60}{2} \\  & =-30.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the rate of change of temperature at the instant of time $t=2$ is $-30{\,}^{∘}\text{C}$ per hour.
